post.summary: Approve one proposed change and apply it
post.description: Re-validates the action's arguments against CURRENT state before executing, so an approval granted minutes ago cannot act on since-deleted data. Once nothing in the run is still undecided the agent resumes and its follow-up turn is returned as `message`. A failure to execute is reported in `error` rather than thrown — the approval was legitimate, the world simply moved on.

200.description: The decided action, plus Ada's follow-up turn when the run resumed.

error.description: Set when execution failed after approval.

404.description: No such action for this user.

409.description: The action has already been decided.

post.description: Nothing is written. The agent resumes once the run has nothing left undecided and adapts rather than re-proposing.

200.description: The declined action, plus Ada's follow-up turn when the run resumed.

404.description: No such action for this user.

409.description: The action has already been decided.

post.description: Corrected from the generated 201: nothing is created.

post.summary: Approve or decline every outstanding change in a conversation
post.description: Applied in proposal order, not concurrently: a plan often creates a subject and then tasks against it, so running them in parallel would race.

approve.description: true applies them all, false declines them all.

200.description: Every decided action, and any follow-up turns the resumed runs produced.

post.description: Corrected from the generated 201: nothing is created, an existing row is flagged inactive.

get.summary: What Ada has stored about this user
get.description: Durable facts carried into every conversation. `source` distinguishes what the user stated outright from what Ada inferred — the pair a user most needs to tell apart when deciding what to remove.

200.description: Stored memories, grouped by kind then most recently updated.

404.description: No such memory for this user.

get.summary: Changes Ada has proposed and is waiting on
get.description: Every create/update/delete the agent wants to make is parked here until the user approves it. Nothing in the user's data has changed while an action is `pending`.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: Limit to one conversation. Omit for everything outstanding.

post.description: Debug-only Cloud SQL smoke test. Creates a table and inserts 5 rows.

get.summary: Completed focus sessions in a date window
get.description: The table was write-only over the wire: every duration, time of day, Prism mode and end mood went in and nothing came back. Completed sessions only, newest first - which is the shape of focus_sessions_user_completed_started_idx, so this is an index scan rather than the seq scan an unfiltered read would be.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to six days before `to`.

200.description: Completed sessions in the window, newest first. Capped at 500 rows.

items.description: The object POST /v1/focus-sessions returns, plus started_at.

422.description: Malformed date, `from` after `to`, or a window wider than 92 days. A wide window is refused rather than silently truncated.

post.description:
Manually trigger the reminder sweep for the current user (test/debug).
 `?force=morning|review` bypasses the time-of-day match.

get.summary: Every fact the weekly report draws, in one read
get.description: One endpoint rather than five composed client-side: the report is a single screen that must appear all at once, and has_activity has to be decided from the union of every kind of evidence in one place - split across endpoints, any disagreement between the two draws a day someone worked as empty.

parameters.name: week_start
parameters.description: Any date inside the week (YYYY-MM-DD); the server snaps to Monday. Defaults to the current week.

get.description: Minimal Prometheus-format metrics (§4.8). Expand with OTel later.

Readiness — dependencies reachable. 503 if DB or Redis is down (Cloud Run
 gates traffic on this).

delete.summary: Remove every microstep from a task occurrence
delete.description: Backs the breakdown toggle in the task editor: switching it off has to take the existing microsteps away, or the switch reads "off" while the plan still shows them and the next save appends a second set. Idempotent - deleting from a task with no steps returns `deleted: 0`. For a repeating occurrence the steps live on the row that the breakdown materialised for that date, and only that date is affected.

parameters.name: occ
parameters.description: Task id, or `<task-id>@<YYYY-MM-DD>` for one occurrence of a repeating task.

404.description: No such task for this user.

patch.summary: Tick a micro-step off, or un-tick it
patch.description: There was previously no way to complete a micro-step: the rows rendered a circle that looked tappable and did nothing, so a breakdown could be read but never worked through. `done` is explicit rather than a server-side toggle, so a retried request cannot flip the step back. The step must belong to the given occurrence - for a repeating task that means the row the breakdown materialised for that date.

parameters.name: occ
parameters.description: Task id, or `<task-id>@<YYYY-MM-DD>` for one occurrence of a repeating task.

404.description: No such step on this occurrence for this user.

info.title: Aqademiq API
info.description: NestJS backend — /v1, snake_case. Auth: custom RS256 JWT (Bearer).

AdaActionFieldDto.description: One line of the before/after diff shown on a confirmation card.

from.description: Absent when the field is being set for the first time.

AdaPendingActionDto.description: A change Ada wants to make, waiting on the user's decision.

message_id.description: The assistant message whose card this is.

warning.description: Irreversible or wide-reaching effects, and scheduling clashes. Shown in red.

AdaMemoryDto.description: One durable fact Ada holds about the user, across conversations.

kind.description: preference = how they like to work; constraint = a fixed commitment; pattern = something observed repeatedly; goal = what they are working toward; fact = durable context.

subject_id.description: Set when the memory applies to one subject only.

source.description: `user` = they stated it outright. `ada` = inferred from behaviour, so weaker — surface this distinction in the UI.

AdaMessageDto.description: One turn in an Ada conversation.

plan.description: Legacy pre-agent propose_plan payload; drives the "Add to my plan" button.

WeeklyReportDayDto.description: One band of the core. Always seven of these, Monday first.

mood_index.description: 0-4 on the shipped ramp, or null when nothing was logged. NOTE: 0 is a real mood and is falsy - a truthiness check here turns the worst day someone logged into a day they did not log.

has_activity.description: A UNION, not an activity-ledger lookup: true if the day carries a ledger row OR a completed task OR a focus session OR a mood check-in. Reading the ledger alone was measured to miss 31 of the 48 days on which someone finished a focus session, across 23 users.

is_future.description: A day later in the week than today. Not active and NOT a gap - drawing it as "nothing logged" tells someone on Thursday that they already missed Friday, Saturday and Sunday.

WeeklyReportDto.description: Facts only. No sentence, label or adjective crosses the wire - all copy is templated client-side where a banned-vocabulary lint can see it as a string literal.

shape.description: The shape of the week, classified from WHICH days carried work and never from how much. A shape drawn from volume ranks days against each other, so one thin day would drag the whole description down.

active_days.description: The hero numeral: days THIS WEEK that carried work, 0-7. A weekly report whose headline is a lifetime total is not a weekly report.

days_on_board.description: Lifetime days on the board. Kept because it is the only count here that cannot go down; deliberately not headlined.

name.description: Null when the subject was deleted after the work happened. It keeps its share; the client draws an unlabelled outline and never names it in copy.

moment.description: One concrete thing that happened - a named task on a named day, never an aggregate.

recovery.description: Null rather than negative. The card is positive-only and the enforcement is server-side, so the number simply does not exist when it points the wrong way. Do not synthesise one from before_avg/after_avg.

held_minutes.description: Paused minutes, reported as a kept quantity.

rhythm_weekdays.description: Weekdays (1-7) that reliably carry work. Empty until there are 3+ weeks of history, which is most accounts.

elapsed_days.description: Days the week has had so far - 4 on a Thursday, 7 once it is over. `shape` is classified against these, not against seven.
